title: Send only the fields that changed in a PATCH request
examObjective: Predicting the result of core DataWeave functions
basics: `filterObject` keeps the key-value pairs of an Object that pass a test. The lambda receives the value and then the key, so `(v, k) -> ...` can look the same key up in another Object with `other[k]`.
prompt:
A form sends `{ before, after }`: the record as it was loaded and as it is being saved. The API only accepts a PATCH body with the fields that changed.

Return an object with every field of `after` whose value differs from `before`, plus every field that was in `before` but has been removed from `after`, with the value `null`.
hints: Two parts: fields of `after` that changed or are new, and fields of `before` that are gone.
In `filterObject ((v, k) -> ...)`, `payload.before[k]` looks up the same key in the other object.
For the removed fields, filter `before` for keys that `after` does not have, and map their values to null.

mustFail.why: compares only the fields of after, so a field that was deleted never reaches the PATCH body
mustFail.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
payload.after filterObject ((v, k) -> payload.before[k] != v)

mustFail.why: selects before.k literally instead of the key held in k, so every field looks changed
mustFail.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
payload.after filterObject ((v, k) -> payload.before.k != v)

explanation.approach: Walking `after` finds the changed and new fields, but a deleted field is not in `after` at all, so it has to be found by walking `before` the other way. `payload.before[k]` uses the key held in `k`; `payload.before.k` asks for a field literally named "k".
